record.original_question: Fix k >= 2 and assume m is sufficiently large. If G is F_{2k+1}-free or F_{2k+2}-free, must lambda(G) be at most (k - 1 + sqrt(4m - k^2 + 1)) / 2, with equality only for K_k joined with an independent set of size m/k - (k - 1)/2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.34 (Yu, Li and Peng [42], 2025). Let k >= 2 be fixed and m be sufficiently large. If G in G(m, F2k+1) or G in G(m, F2k+2), then lambda(G) <= (k-1+sqrt(4m-k^2+1))/2.
Hence, Conjecture 3.34 follows directly from Theorems 3.32 and 3.35.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer n ≥ 3, the fan graph F_n is defined as the join K_1 ∨ P_{n-1}, that is, the graph obtained from a path on n−1 vertices by adding a single new vertex adjacent to every vertex of the path. For a graph H, a graph G is called H-free if G contains no subgraph isomorphic to H. Let G(m, H) denote the family of all H-free simple graphs with exactly m edges. For a graph G, let λ(G) denote the spectral radius (the largest eigenvalue) of its adjacency matrix. The join G_1 ∨ G_2 of two graphs is obtained by taking their disjoint union and adding all edges between V(G_1) and V(G_2). Let K_k denote the complete graph on k vertices and let tK_1 denote the empty graph on t vertices.

Prove or disprove the following statement. Fix an integer k ≥ 2. There exists m_0 = m_0(k) such that for every integer m ≥ m_0, every graph G ∈ G(m, F_{2k+1}) ∪ G(m, F_{2k+2}) satisfies
   λ(G) ≤ (k − 1 + √(4m − k^2 + 1)) / 2,
and equality holds if and only if G is isomorphic to K_k ∨ ((m/k − (k−1)/2) K_1).
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate the conjecture has been resolved. Li et al. established the result for k ≥ 3, while the remaining case k = 2 was handled in two parts: the F_5 case was settled by Yu et al., and the F_6 case was resolved in subsequent work determining the maximum spectral radius of F_6-free graphs with m ≥ 88 edges. Together these results cover all cases of the conjecture.
